text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Albanian President Sali Berisha called on the opposition Socialist Party to take up their seats in parliament.
- A group within the ruling Democratic Party, which has a more than comfortable majority in parliament, has been going against party leadership.

- The pretender to the Albanian throne has told the mayor of Shkoder, a member of his monarchy party, he would help the city financially and repeated his appeal a referendum should be held to decide the form of regime in Albania.
- Fatos Nano, the jailed leader of the opposition Socialist Party, has been receiving 100 letters and postcards a day from all over the world.
- The manager of an alleged pyramid scheme has postponed for the second time payments to thousands of creditors.
- Parliament has approved a seven-member commission to investigate the activity of alleged pyramid schemes.
- Vefa Holding, Albania's biggest concern, will lower its monthly dividend to five percent to secure stability for investors over a longer period of time.
- A 15-year-old girl has won Albania's national song contest.
- The Gjallica company, which gives 10 percent interest on money deposited, has told worried depositors that it just halting business for three days due to "small problems".
- Albania's parliament has approved tougher laws for convicted killers, rapers, smugglers, tax dodgers and corrupt officials.
